title: Unauthorized Account Takeover During Device Enrollment
description: An attacker could impersonate the Homeowner to register and enroll cameras/sensors in their account, gaining control over the IoT system.
assumptions: Attacker has access to Homeowner's credentials or can intercept authentication during enrollment process.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a reasonable assumption for ExternalEntity->Process usurpation threat.

title: Homeowner Data Disclosure During Account Registration
description: Personal information provided during account registration (name, address, contact details) could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties.
assumptions: Data transmission or storage during enrollment is not adequately protected.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 applies to source/flow disclosure in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Homeowner Identification from Enrollment Data
description: The Homeowner could be identified from their device enrollment records, potentially revealing their home location and security setup.
assumptions: Enrollment data contains identifiable information that can be linked to the Homeowner.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is standard for identification threats at source in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Linkability of Homeowner to Device Usage Patterns
description: The Homeowner's identity could be linked to their device usage patterns, revealing when and how they interact with their home security system.
assumptions: System logs or metadata can be correlated to identify the Homeowner's behavior.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 applies to linkability threats at source in ExternalEntity->Process flows.

title: Access Code Disclosure to Unauthorized Parties
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest user could be logged, transmitted, or stored in a way that exposes it to unauthorized parties, potentially allowing code reuse or tracking of guest access patterns.
assumptions: The system logs access codes or transmits them over networks without adequate encryption or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard smart home hub behavior where access codes may be logged for audit purposes.

title: Linkability of Guest Access to Identity
description: An observer could potentially link the guest's access code entry to their identity through metadata (timestamp, location, device) or by observing the guest at the door, creating a profile of guest visitation patterns.
assumptions: Access logs contain timestamps and potentially other identifying metadata that could be correlated with guest identity.
uncertainty_note: Depends on what metadata is actually logged by the Home Hub system.

title: Usurpation of Guest Access Code
description: An attacker could observe or intercept the temporary access code as the guest enters it, allowing unauthorized access to the home. Shoulder surfing or network interception could enable this.
assumptions: The access code is entered in a visible manner or transmitted over an unencrypted channel.
uncertainty_note: Likelihood depends on physical security of the entry point and network security of the hub.

title: Detection of Guest Presence via System Response
description: The Home Hub's response (e.g., door unlock, status indicator, notification) could reveal to observers that a guest is present or attempting to access the home, even without direct observation of the guest.
assumptions: System responses (lights, sounds, status indicators) are observable from outside or by neighbors.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific design of the Home Hub's response mechanisms.

title: Linkability of Event Log Entries
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could link individual motion/door/sensor events together to reconstruct detailed patterns of household activity, potentially revealing routines, presence, and behavior.
assumptions: Attacker has physical or network access to the local event log storage.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Data
description: Motion, door, and sensor events could be used to identify specific individuals or their presence in the home, potentially revealing who is present, when they enter/leave, and their activities.
assumptions: Event data contains sufficient contextual information (timestamps, sensor types) to infer individual presence or identity.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a general identification node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Log Data
description: If the local event log is accessible to unauthorized parties (e.g., through physical access, network compromise, or insecure storage), sensitive household activity data could be disclosed.
assumptions: Event log is stored locally without adequate access controls or encryption.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Data Manipulation of Event Log
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could alter, delete, or inject false events, compromising the integrity of the household monitoring system.
assumptions: Event log is stored without write protection or integrity checks.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a general data manipulation node; specific LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Linkability of camera footage across sessions
description: Cloud video storage may allow linking of video clips from different time periods, potentially revealing patterns of home occupancy and activities.
assumptions: Cloud storage system maintains metadata that enables temporal correlation of video clips.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Identifiability of individuals in video footage
description: Recorded camera clips can identify individuals (homeowners, visitors, family members) within the home environment, creating privacy risks if accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Video footage contains recognizable human subjects and identifiable locations.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored video data
description: Cloud video storage may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, leading to disclosure of sensitive home surveillance footage to third parties.
assumptions: Cloud storage system has potential security vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Usurpation of legitimate data access
description: Unauthorized actors may gain access to cloud video storage and impersonate legitimate users to access or manipulate stored surveillance footage.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Excessive motion data disclosure to backend
description: Home Hub (P1) forwards real-time motion alert data to Mobile App Backend (P2), potentially disclosing personal data beyond what's strictly necessary. Motion data may contain location patterns, activity timing, or behavioral information that exceeds minimal disclosure requirements.
assumptions: Motion alert data contains personal information; the transfer to backend is not strictly necessary for the intended function
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.4 from context [5] as it addresses excessive exposure to known parties (backend system). The exact nature of motion data's personal content is inferred from typical smart home contexts.

title: Linkability of motion detection events to homeowner behavior patterns
description: Motion-detected notifications could be linked to other data about the homeowner's activities, location, or presence patterns, potentially revealing behavioral profiles or routines.
assumptions: The system collects or stores additional data about the homeowner that could be correlated with motion events.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of motion detection data
description: Motion detection notifications could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties if the notification system or homeowner's device is compromised.
assumptions: The notification transmission or storage is vulnerable to interception or unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Excessive data in motion detection notification
description: The notification may contain more data than necessary (e.g., precise location, timestamp, camera feed) violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The notification includes detailed information beyond what is needed to alert the homeowner of motion.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on general LINDDUN methodology; exact node may vary by implementation.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor may contain patterns or metadata that could be linked with other datasets to re-identify individual users or correlate with other privacy-sensitive information.
assumptions: Vendor may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with this analytics data
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as it's a common linkability node; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Cloud analytics vendor may share or sell the received analytics data to unauthorized third parties, violating the intended scope of data sharing.
assumptions: Vendor may have weak contractual controls or may monetize the data beyond agreed terms
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 selected as it represents disclosure at the flow destination

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: Analytics data could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission to the cloud vendor, leading to inaccurate reporting or malicious manipulation of usage statistics.
assumptions: Transmission channel may lack adequate encryption or integrity verification
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 represents data integrity threat at the flow level

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with external vendor may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, or cross-border transfer requirements are not met.
assumptions: Data may contain residual PII or be transferred across jurisdictions without proper safeguards
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 selected for non-compliance at the external entity receiving data

title: Unauthorized access to video playback data
description: Mobile app backend (P2) retrieves video clips from cloud storage (DS2) for playback. If access controls are insufficient, unauthorized users or processes could access video data that should be restricted to the homeowner.
assumptions: Access controls on the mobile app backend are not properly implemented or are bypassed
uncertainty_note: Using generic D.1.1.1 node as specific tree node not provided in context

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage (DS2) may be retained longer than necessary for the playback service, violating data minimization and storage limitation principles under privacy regulations.
assumptions: No clear retention policy exists for video clips in the cloud storage
uncertainty_note: Context [4] provides Nc.1.1.4 node for storage limitation, but specific application to this flow requires assumption about retention policies

title: Unauthorized use of video playback data
description: Video clips retrieved by mobile app backend (P2) could be used for purposes beyond the intended playback service, such as analytics, training, or sharing with third parties without homeowner consent.
assumptions: No explicit consent mechanism or usage restrictions are enforced on retrieved video data
uncertainty_note: Generic U.1.1.1 node used as specific tree node not provided in context
